description: A finished orbital courier game with six authored contracts, realistic two-body maneuver planning, rendezvous, a flight advisor, fuel and time medals, rewinds, a seeded dispatch board, and unlimited free flight.
features: Six complete contracts: apogee raising, circular transfer, eccentric buoy deployment, phased relay rendezvous, retrograde return, and hyperbolic escape
Instantaneous transverse/radial maneuvers with editable departure time, apsis presets, exact numeric inputs, sliders, and an on-map drag handle
Current and predicted conics, destination geometry, orbital telemetry, burn cost, C3, and future relay closest approach
Canvas 2D Earth and orbital map, procedural stars, apsis markers, zoom, fit, grid toggle, thruster feedback, and completion particles
Pause, four time-warp speeds, apsis coasting, mission recall, restart, unlimited pre-burn rewinds, and flight recorder
Three seals per campaign contract for completion, delta-v efficiency, and timing; best results retained only for the current visit
Contextual pilot notebook with computed conventional-transfer suggestions and detailed learning/control/model manual
Seeded dispatch board with repeatable route codes and free flight at four selectable altitudes
Responsive layouts, keyboard shortcuts, labeled form inputs, focus-contained dialogs, reduced-motion CSS, optional synthesized sound, and no-Canvas fallback

architecture.rendering: Canvas 2D with CSS/HTML UI; no WebGL needed
architecture.physics: Bracketed universal-variable Kepler propagation with Stumpff functions, instantaneous orthonormal radial/transverse impulses

assumptions: Planar Newtonian two-body motion around a stationary spherical Earth; mu 398600.4418 km^3/s^2 and radius 6371 km.
Internal units are kilometers, seconds, and km/s; UI impulses use m/s. Transverse and radial axes are perpendicular; transverse is not velocity-aligned away from apsides.
Burns are instantaneous impulses against an abstract delta-v budget. No thrust duration, propellant mass, rocket equation, or spacecraft attitude dynamics.
No atmosphere/drag, J2, Sun/Moon perturbations, Earth rotation, inclination, relativistic corrections, launch, landing, or reentry.
The flight is recalled at the 100 km atmospheric safety boundary. Event checks occur at no more than 20 simulated seconds, plus an apsidal crossing guard.
Orbital-shape contracts certify osculating apsides without requiring physical arrival at the far point. Escape requires reaching the release altitude outbound.
Station capture uses a forgiving 50 km and 60 m/s gameplay envelope. Real docking is much more demanding.
Orbit distances have one linear scale; spacecraft and station symbols are enlarged. Canvas 2D replaces any need for WebGL.
Progress is memory-only and resets on reload. No backend, accounts, analytics, storage, or runtime network requests.
limitations: This is a learning game, not operational mission planning or navigation software.
Nearest-pass search is sampled and refined over a bounded future interval of at most four hours, not a global rendezvous optimizer.
The notebook assumes conventional transfers. After large off-plan maneuvers, manual correction or rewind may be required.
Safety boundary and goal recognition can occur up to one 20-second event interval after first crossing.
A no-Canvas browser retains the flight controls and numerical game, but cannot display the orbital map.
